answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 29 answers need 29 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the hollow index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the kernel audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the bridge identifier and voids the later submissions, as a result the operator pays for 29 runs and collects one. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
